Antalya and Corycus in Anatolia are briefly annexed by the Kingdom of Cyprus.
The Venetian government forces Catherine to cede her rights over Cyprus because she had no heir. The rule of the Lusignan dynasty comes to an end after nearly three centuries.
Ottoman Turks raid the Karpasia Peninsula.
Ottoman Turks attack Limassol.
Ottoman army besieges Nicosia.
A period of Ottoman occupation of the island begins, during which twenty-eight bloody uprisings will occur.

The Chronological History of the island of Cyprus, later described as "the only scholarly monograph of modern Greek literature since the fall of Constantinople", is published by Kyprianos Kouriokourineos, one of the most prominent Greek-Cypriot intellectuals and clerics of the 18th century.
The Suez Canal opened.
Sir Garnet Joseph Wolseley became Crown commissioner.
Sir Robert Biddulph became Crown commissioner.
Sir Henry Ernest Bulwer became Crown commissioner.
Sir Walter Sendall became Crown commissioner.
Sir William Frederick Haynes-Smith became Crown commissioner.
Sir Charles King-Harman became Crown commissioner.
Sir Hamilton Goold-Adams became Crown commissioner.
Sir John Eugene Clauson became Crown commissioner.
Sir Malcolm Stevenson became Crown commissioner.
Sir Ronald Storrs became governor.
Sir Reginald Edward Stubbs became governor.
Sir Herbert Richmond Palmer became governor.
Cypriots fought with the British in World War II, Greek Cypriots demanding Enosis at war's end. The Turkish Cypriots wanted British rule to continue.
Sir William Denis Battershill became governor.
Sir Charles Campbell Woolley became governor.
Sir Reginald Fletcher, Lord Winster, became governor.
The British Government finished imprisoning displaced Jews.
Sir Andrew Barkworth Wright became governor.
Sir Robert Perceval Armitage became governor.

Minister of State for the Colonies, Henry Hopkinson, says that there were certain territories in the Commonwealth 'which, owing to their particular circumstances, can never expect to be fully independent'.
Sir John Harding became governor.
Field Marshal Sir John Harding was replaced by the civilian governor Sir Hugh Foot in a conciliatory move.
First of 2 days of serious rioting by Turkish Cypriots. Seven were killed by British security forces.

Turkish press office in Nicosia is bombed. Inter-communal clashes as Turkish Cypriots invade Greek sector. On 26 June 1984 the Turkish Cypriot leader, Rauf Denktaş, admitted on British channel ITV that the bomb was placed by the Turks themselves in order to create tension. On 9 January 1995 Rauf Denktaş repeated his claim in the Turkish newspaper, Milliyet.

The first massacre between Greeks and Turks on Cyprus. British police released from arrest a group of 35 Greeks in the region of Guenyeli. A Turkish mob attacks the unarmed group, killing some of them.

British minesweeper HMS Burmaston intercepts the Turkish registered boat, Deniz. Loaded with weaponry, the boat is scuttled by its 3-member crew. The crew, all Turkish nationals, are arrested for importing munitions without a permit.
Archbishop Makarios III and Dr. Fazıl Küçük appeal to their respective communities to hand over illegal weapons.
Deadline to hand over illegal weapons.
British occupation ended.

The Battle of Tylliria takes place. Greek-Cypriot forces storm the Turkish-held Kokkina enclave, prompting a Turkish military intervention and airstrikes on the Greek forces. However, Soviet pressure prevented the Turks from going any further, and when the battle ended after four days of fierce fighting, the Kokkina enclave had been reduced to 50-40% of its original size.
EOKA B' is being created
The Turks emerged from their enclaves.
UN sponsored talks began between the two sides.
The UN talks ran into the sand, but with a commitment to resume.
The European Court of Human Rights found Turkey guilty of continuing human rights violations against the Greek Cypriots.
Cyprus was set to join the European Union in May 2004. Renewed negotiations about the status of the island took place.

Demetris Christofias replaced Tassos Papadopoulos as president of the Republic of Cyprus. It was the first time that a leader of the Greek Cypriot communist party, AKEL, had entered the presidential race. He was at the time the only communist leader in the European Union.
Legendary establishment of Tamna by Go, Yang, and Bu on Jeju Island.
Historian Richard McBride posits that the historical founding of Old Chosŏn as a polity likely began around this time.
Estimated beginning of the Gojoseon-Yan War that eventually ends in Gojoseon's loss of the Liaodong peninsula to Yan.
Establishment of Jin in southern Korean peninsula.
Buyeo, which Goguryeo and Baekje claim descent from, is established sometime around the 2nd century BC.
The oldest known Korean song, Song of the Yellow Bird is written by Yuri of Goguryeo.
Goguryeo begins to become a centralized kingdom under Taejo's reign.
Baekje begins to become a centralized kingdom under Goi's reign.
Goguryeo is defeated by Cao Wei in the Goguryeo–Wei War.
Silla becomes a centralized kingdom under Naemul's reign.
Baekje's King Geunchogo invades Goguryeo and kills King Gogugwon.
Sosurim also establishes Korea's first National Confucian Academy.
Chimnyu of Baekje officially adopts Buddhism.
Last remains of Buyeo absorbed by Goguryeo.
Baekje attacks Tamna (modern-day Jeju Province), which enters into a tributary relationship with Baekje as a result.
Silla vassalizes Usan (modern-day Ulleungdo).
Baekje moves its capital to Sabi (modern-day Buyeo).
Silla attacks Baekje, breaking the alliance.
First of a series of major Sui dynasty attacks in the Goguryeo–Sui War, which ends in 614 in a costly defeat for Sui.
Goguryeo repulses second Sui invasion at the Salsu.
Goguryeo builds the first Cheolli Jangseong following Tang incursions into Goguryeo's northwestern border.
First campaign in the Goguryeo–Tang War.
Silla establishes alliance with Tang.
As a result of the fall of Baekje, Tamna enters into a tributary relationship with Silla.
Battle of Baekgang, the remnants of Baekje allied with Japanese expeditionary forces are defeated by the Silla-Tang alliance, ending all hopes for the restoration of the kingdom.
Goguryeo falls to the Silla-Tang forces.
Silla repels Chinese forces from the Korean peninsula, completes unification of much of the Three Kingdoms following the Silla-Tang War and successfully defends its independence.
Balhae reaches its peak under King Seon of Balhae.
Silla formally surrenders to Goryeo.
Hubaekje formally surrenders to Goryeo.
Tae Kwanghyŏn, the last Crown Prince of Balhae, flees to Goryeo with a great portion of the Balhae royalty and aristocracy and settles with tens of thousands of Balhae households there.
Goryeo subjugates Tamna.
According to the Goryeosa, tens of thousands of Balhae refugees from Jeongan flee to Goryeo, marking the largest Balhae migration since the 936 exodus.
Jeongan falls to the Liao Dynasty.
The second ravages the northern border.
Buddhist monk and geomancer Myocheong rebels in a failed attempt to move the capital to Pyongyang and pursue aggressive expansion against the Jin Dynasty.
Goryeo helps the Mongol Empire during the Mongol invasions of Japan.
The First Strife of the Princes occurs.
The capital is moved back to Kaesong.
The Second Strife of the Princes [ko] occurs.
Paper currency initiated
The capital is moved back to Hanyang.
The palace Changdeokgung is established in Hanyang.
Namdaemun Market, now the oldest extant market in Korea, is established.
The government research institute Hall of Worthies is established.
Goryeosa compiled.
Two fires destroy much of Hanyang.

Local nobleman Yi Ŭngt'ae dies, leaving a pregnant widow and a child named Wŏn behind. His widow leaves a grief-stricken letter in his tomb that is later discovered in 1998 and becomes famous internationally.
4th month. All the palaces in Seoul are burnt down.
The Chŏngyu War begins.
The war causes the Kyegap Famine (계갑대기근; 癸甲大飢饉) to begin. It lasts until 1594.
António Corea, a Korean slave kidnapped and taken to Japan, is sold to an Italian master. He is then taken to Italy at latest by 1600, and becomes possibly the first Korean to set foot in Europe.
Pyŏngjŏng Famine (병정대기근; 丙丁大飢饉).
The Later Jin invasion of Joseon occurs.
A crop failure leds to famine that lasts until 1815 and kills around 2,000,000.
A Moment mag. scale"}]]}'>Mw 7.3 earthquake strikes present-day North Hamgyong Province, damaging towns and killing residents.
Famine in northern Korea that causes Koreans to flee to Russia.
The palace Gyeongbokgung is reconstructed after having been abandoned since the Imjin War.
10 December. Japanese newspaper Chōsen shinpō becomes the first newspaper to be published in Korea.

July to October. The first Korean diplomatic mission to the United States also gives rise to the first Koreans to set foot in North America, the first Korean to study abroad in the United States (Yu Kil-chun), and the first Koreans to circumnavigate the globe (Min Yong Ik [ko], Pyŏn Su [ko], and Soh Kwang-pom).
31 October. The first native Korean newspaper, Hansŏng sunbo, is established by the Joseon monarchy. It is written in Classical Chinese.

11 October. The first Methodist church in Korea, Chungdong First Methodist Church, is established. The church's main chapel, built in 1897, is now the oldest extant church in Korea, and the only extant one built in the 19th century.
25th day, 1st month. The government newspaper Hansŏng jubo is established. It is the first newspaper written primarily in the Korean language (mixed script) and the first weekly newspaper in Korea.
Ae Kwan Theater, the first movie theater in Korea, is established in Incheon.
April. After Japanese victory in the Sino–Japanese War, China recognizes Korean independence in the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
1 January. Joseon begins to use the Gregorian calendar.
11 February. Gojong's internal exile to the Russian legation.
20 February. King Gojong leaves the Russian legation and makes Deoksugung his official palace.
18 July. Landmark newspaper The Korea Daily News, predecessor to today's Seoul Shinmun, is founded by British journalist Ernest Bethell.
Philip Jaisohn becomes the first ethnic Korean to obtain a Western doctorate degree.
Imun Seolnongtang, now the oldest continually operating restaurant in South Korea, opens around this time in Seoul.
8 May. Koreans arrive in Mexico for the first time.
Treaty of Portsmouth ends the Russo-Japanese War in Russian defeat and leads to uncontested Japanese dominance of Korean politics
Kim Ransa becomes the first Korean woman to receive a bachelor's degree from the United States.
1 September. The historic Japanese newspaper in Korea Keijō nippō is founded. The newspaper becomes the de facto official paper of the Japanese Residency-General and later Government-General.
February. The National Debt Repayment Movement begins. It ends by 1908.
9 September – 15 November. The Kyŏngsŏng Exhibition (경성박람회; 京城博覽會) is held in Seoul.
23 March. Durham Stevens, an American diplomat and Japanese sympathizer, is assassinated by Korean independence activists.
15 October. The first Korean-owned private regional newspaper Gyeongnam Ilbo is established.
6 June. The Battle of Samdunja occurs between Korean rebels and the Empire of Japan.
7 June. The Battle of Fengwudong occurs between Korean rebels and the Empire of Japan.
26 October. The Battle of Qingshanli between the Imperial Japanese Army and the Korean Independence Army (led by Kim Chwajin) takes place. Both sides claim victory.
17 August. The Seishin Operation is fought between the Soviet Union and Japan, with the Soviets winning.
Qin armies evict Xiongnu nomadic tribes from their pastures on the Yellow River in the Ordos Loop. Xiongnu leader Touman forced to flee far into the Mongolian Plateau.
Modu Chanyu found the Xiongnu Empire. These nomadic peoples would inhabit the eastern Asian Steppe from the 3rd century BCE to the late 1st century CE.
Xiongnu launch second war against the Yuezhi, seizing a large swath of Yuezhi territory (modern day Xinjiang).
At the Battle of Baideng, Emperor Gaozu of Han was ambushed reputedly by 300,000 elite Xiongnu cavalry, only narrowly escaping capture.
Modu Chanyu and the emperor Gaozu of China's Han dynasty sign a peace treaty, recognizing equality of the Xiongnu.
Modu Chanyu leads a Xiongnu invasion of the Gansu region and soundly defeats last remnants of the Yuezhi, killing the Yuezhi king in the process and asserting their presence in the Western Regions.
Death of Xiongnu leader Modu Chanyu.
The Battle of Mayi, an abortive ambush operation by Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi) against the invading Xiongnu forces, begins a decades-long Han dynasty offensive against the nomads.

The Battle of Mobei, Han forces invade the northern regions of the Gobi Desert forcing the Xiongnu to flee into Siberia. After a series of further defeats, the Xiongnu are expelled from the Ordos Desert and Qilian Mountains.
Various tribes invade the Xiongnu territory from all fronts; Wusun from the west, Dingling from the north, Wuhuan from the east, and Han forces from the south.
Xiongnu civil war as factions fight for power following the death of Xulüquanqu, the 12th Chanyu
The southern Xiongnu surrender and become tributaries to the Han after splitting into northern and southern dynasties.

At the Battle of Zhizhi General Chen Tang and Protector General Gan Yanshou, acting without explicit permission from the Han court, kill Northern Xiongnu leader Zhizhi Chanyu at his capital city (present-day Taraz, Kazakhstan)
Tsi Yung, allied with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, attacked the northern Xiongnu kingdom. Xianbei move into Xiongnu territory.
The Xianbei successfully repel an invasion of the Han dynasty.
The Xianbei conquer areas of northern China.

The last khagan of the Xianbei, Kebineng, is assassinated by Cao Wei, successor state of the Eastern Han (25–220). The Xianbei state disintegrates into a number of smaller independent domains (Murong, Tuoba, Khitan people, Shiwei, and Rouran Khaganate).
The Chinese Northern Qi and Northern Zhou dynasties begin paying tribute to the Göktürks.
Turkic Khaganate revolts against Emperor of Sui and besiege the command seats at present-day Daixian in Shanxi
A Tang army under the command of Li Jing defeats the Eastern Turkic Khaganate under the command of Illig Qaghan at the Battle of Yinshan

A reunited China—under the Tang dynasty (618–906) destroys the Eastern Türk north of the Gobi and establishes the Anbei Protectorate in the Mongolian Steppes. Uyghurs khagan are installed as Anbei protector.
Ilterish Qaghan of the Second Turkic Khaganate dies and is succeeded by his brother Qapaghan Qaghan.
Qapaghan Qaghan of the Second Turkic Khaganate defeats the Khitans to the east and raids the Tang dynasty.
Qapaghan Qaghan of the Second Turkic Khaganate defeats the Turgesh
The Basmyl, Uyghurs, and Karluks revolt against the Second Turkic Khaganate
Uyghurs destroy several northern Yenisei Kyrgyz trading outposts before slaughtering a Kyrgyz army and executing their Khan
The Khitan ruled eastern Mongolia, most of Manchuria, and much of China north of the Yellow River.
Emperor Taizong launches an invasion of the Jin.
Khitan chieftains had established themselves as emperors of northern China. The Khitan state is renamed the Liao dynasty
Emperor Shizong of Liao is murdered by a relative and is succeeded by Yelü Jing, son of Emperor Taizong of Liao, who becomes Emperor Muzong of Liao
Zhao Kuangyin declares himself Emperor Taizu of Song, replacing Later Zhou
Liao dynasty assists Northern Han in repelling Song dynasty
Emperor Muzong of Liao is murdered by his attendants and is succeeded by Yelü Xian, son of Emperor Shizong of Liao, who becomes Emperor Jingzong of Liao
Liao dynasty attempts to assist Northern Han in repelling Song dynasty but is defeated at the Battle of Gaoliang River
Emperor Jingzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Longxu succeeds him as Emperor Shengzong of Liao; Empress Xiao Yanyan becomes regent
The Liao dynasty reverts to calling itself the Khitans
First conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War: Khitans invade Goryeo and acquire nominal tributary status over Goryeo

Emperor Shengzong of Liao conducts a full-scale invasion of the Song dynasty which ends in stalemate and the Chanyuan Treaty, an agreement to an annual payment of silk and silver from the Song to the Khitans
Empress Xiao Yanyan dies
Second conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War: Mokjong of Goryeo is murdered by Kang Cho and the Khitans send an expedition to punish him; Kang Cho is killed
Third conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War: Khitans invade Goryeo but are defeated
Third conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War: Khitans prepares another army to attack Goryeo
Emperor Shengzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Zongzhen succeeds him as Emperor Xingzong of Liao; Empress Dowager Xiao Noujin becomes regent
Emperor Xingzong of Liao dies and is succeeded by his son Yelü Hongji, who becomes Emperor Daozong of LiaoAll officials are required to wear Chinese court dress
Khitans revert to calling their state the Liao dynasty
Unusually heavy snowfall kills 70 percent of livestock and horses
Mogusi of the Zubu and the Dilie tribes of western Heilongjiang raid the Liao dynasty
Emperor Daozong of Liao dies and his grandson Yelü Yanxi succeeds him as Emperor Tianzuo of Liao
Emperor Taizu of Jin defeats the Khitan army of the Liao dynasty

Emperor Tianzuo of Liao flees the Southern Capital and his uncle Yelü Chun is declared emperor of Northern Liao, however he dies three months later and the title is passed down to Yelü Ding, the son in hiding with his father the emperor also in hiding; real power goes to Empress Dowager Xiao Puxiannu
Yelü Dashi annexes two Jin tribes
Yelü Dashi leaves the Orkhon River with 20,000 followers and travels to the Kingdom of Qocho where the ruler welcomes him
Yelü Dashi attacks the Karakhanids at Kashgar but is repelled
Yelü Dashi dies and his wife Xiao Tabuyan succeeds him as regent
Yelü Yilie, son of Yelü Dashi, becomes gurkhan of the Qara Khitai
Ögedei Khan, third son of Temüjin (Genghis Khan) is born.
Temüjin given the title Genghis Khan (Chinggis Khaan), first Khagan (Great Khan) of the Mongol Empire.
Kublai Khan, son of Tolui and grandson of Genghis Khan, is born.
Zhenjin, second son of Kublai Khan and later founder of the Yuan dynasty, is born.
Güyük Khan, third Khagan of the Mongol Empire, dies aged 42.
Möngke Khan, fourth Khagan of the Mongol Empire, dies aged 50.

Kublai Khan, son of Tolui and grandson of Genghis Khan, becomes fifth Khagan of the Mongol Empire. However, the Toluid Civil War begins as various members of the Tolui family line fight for the title of Khagan resulting in the division of the Mongol Empire.
Zhenjin designated Crown Prince by Kublai Khan.
Temür Khan, son of Crown Prince Zhenjin and grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes sixth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and second emperor of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty.

A peace among the Mongol khanates establishes the nominal supremacy of the Yuan dynasty over the three western khanates (the Golden Horde, the Chagatai Khanate and the Ilkhanate). However, the peace itself was short-lived and the war soon resumed.

With the death of Temür Khan (aged 41), Külüg Khan, first son of Darmabala and Dagi of the Khunggirad clan, and a great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes seventh Khagan of the Mongol Empire and third Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

Külüg Khan dies (aged 29). Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan, second son of Darmabala and Dagi of the Khunggirat, and a great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes eighth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and fourth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.
Revival of the imperial examination system within the Yuan dynasty under Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan.
Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan dies (aged 34), Gegeen Khan, eldest son of Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan and Radnashiri, becomes ninth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and fifth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.
Death of Gegeen Khan (aged 20). Yesün Temür, son of Gammala, grandson of Zhenjin and great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes tenth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and sixth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

With the death of Yesün Temür (aged 34), Ragibagh Khan, eldest son of Yesün Temür, becomes 11th Khagan of the Mongol Empire at the age of 7-8 and designated seventh Emperor of the Yuan dynasty before being deposed in a coup before his succession.

Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür, second son of Khayishan, becomes 12th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and eighth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty. The War of the Two Capitals begins. His forces defeated, Ragibagh Khan disappears or dies at the age of 7–8, possibly murdered.

Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür abdicates and his elder brother Khutughtu Khan Kusala becomes 13th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and ninth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty. However, he dies on August 30 at age 28, four days after a banquet with brother Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür, presumed to have been poisoned. Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür regaines the throne on September 8.

With the death of Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür (aged 28), Rinchinbal Khan, second son of Khutughtu Khan Kusala, becomes 14th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and tenth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty at the age of six.

Rinchinbal Khan dies nine months later (aged 6), Toghon Temür, (1320–1370) eldest son of Khutughtu Khan Kusala and older brother of Rinchinbal, becomes 15th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and eleventh Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.
Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara (1340–1378), son of Toghon Temür, is declared Khan of Mongolia at Karakorum. Timur (Tamerlane) gains control of the western Chagatai Khanate.
Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür (1342–1388) succeeds his brother Ayuushridar as Khan of Mongolia.
Elbeg Nigülesügchi Khan (1361–1399) overthrew Engke Khan from the House of Ariq Böke succeeds as Khan of the Mongols.
Timur invades the Golden Horde and sacks Saray and Astrakhan.
Elbeg Nigülesügchi Khagan is defeated by the Four Oirats and killed by their leaders, Ugetchi Khashikha and Batula.
Timur dies of illness at Farab (present day Kazakhstan) while preparing for war against Ming China.
Öljei Temür Khan (1379–1412) succeeds his father Elbeg Nigülesügchi Khan and older brother Gün Temür Khan as Khan of the Yuan dynasty.
Oirat nobles place Oyiradai (died 1425) on the throne of Khagan of the Mongol Khan of the Northern Yuan dynasty following the death of Delbeg Khan
Adai Khan (1390–1438) assumes throne of Northern Yuan dynasty, unifies both the central and eastern Mongol territories but then suffers major defeats by Oirats in 1430 and 1434.
Oirats crown Toghtoa Bukha (Taisun Khan) as Khagan of the Northern Yuan. He later proclaims himself of Khagan of the Great Yuan enraging the Ming dynasty.
Dayan Khan launches successive invasions of China that continue through 1526 and include an unsuccessful assault on Beijing in 1517

Following his brother's death in 1542, Altan Khan (grandson of Dayan Khan) becomes the de facto leader of the whole of the "Right Wing" (western Inner Mongolia and Ordos) and is given the title, "Tüsheet Sechen Khan."
Yonten Gyatso, great-grandson of Altan Khan, becomes the 4th Dalai Lama in Lhasa, Tibet.
Several Mongol tribes defect to the Qing due to Ligdan Khan's oppressive rule.
Ligdan Khan flees to Tibet to evade the Manchus and conquer the Gelug.
Irkutsk fort founded.
Galdan Khan founds the town of Khovd.
The Dzungars invade Khalkha and force Khalkha nobility to flee to Inner Mongolia.
The Khoshut Lha-bzang Khan deposes the Sixth Dalai Lama in Tibet and kills the regent Sangs-rgyas rGya-mtsho.
Khalkha jirum (Khalkha regulations) replaces the Mongol-Oirat Code among the Khalkha Mongols.
Acting on an appeal by the Tibetan monasteries, the Dzungar army occupies Lhasa and kills The Khoshut Lha-bzang Khan.
The Qing armies establish a garrison and military farm near modern Khovd city in western Mongolia.
Qing dynasty's Kangxi Emperor drives Dzungar forces from Tibet.
Death of Zanabazar. Upper Mongols under rule of the prince Lubsan Danzan revolt against the Qing but are defeated.
Dawaachi and Amursanaa overthrow the Dzungar ruler in Xinjiang; Dawaachi becomes new Khong Tayiji (ruler).
The Qing armies occupy Dzungaria in Xinjiang.
Third Jebtsundamba Khutuktu identified in Tibet (first outside of Mongolia)
Qing law replaces the native code, Khalkha jirum.
First tsam religious dances performed in Ikh Khuree
Russian statesman Mikhail Speransky reforms administration of the Buriats and other Indigenous peoples of Siberia.
Opening of the Russian-Mongol school in Kyakhta
The Jebtsundamba Khutuktu relocates from east Khüriye (now central Ulaanbaatar) to Gandantegchinlen (Gandan) Monastery to avoid Chinese merchants.
Completion of Gandantegchinlen (Gandan) Monastery in Ikh Khuree
The Buriat Cossack Dorzhi Banzarov becomes first person of Mongol ancestry to earn a European Ph.D. at University of Kazan in Russia.
Russian Consul takes up residence in Ikh Khuree
Agvaanl Uvsanchoijinyam Danzan Vanchüg is born in Lithang, Kham. He will later be formally installed as the Bogd Khan of the new Mongolian state
Anti-Manchu mutiny by Uliastai garrison
Chinese rebels of the Jindandao (Way of the Golden Pill) sect launch massive pogroms against Mongols in southeastern Inner Mongolia.
Agreement to build a telegraph line from Russia to China via Ikh Khuree. Construction of Trans-Siberian Railway begins.
The Qing government implemented sinification policies.
The Russian Empire recognized Mongolian independence and the rule of Bogd Khan.
Mongolia and Tibet concluded treaty on mutual recognition and mutual assistance.
Roman von Ungern-Sternberg drove Chinese troops out of Niislel Khüree.
The People's Provisional Government of seven men was formed in Soviet Russia.
People's Revolution of 1921: The Russian Red Army, with the support of Damdin Sükhbaatar, defeated the forces of Ungern-Sternberg.
Ungern-Sternberg was captured by a Soviet detachment.
The show trial of Ungern sentenced him to execution by firing squad. Ungern was shot the following night.
High-ranking figures, accused of anti-revolutionary conspiracy by Soliin Danzan, were shot dead. Notable victims included Dogsomyn Bodoo, Dambyn Chagdarjav, and Ja Lama.
Revolutionary commander Damdin Sükhbaatar mysteriously passed away. Rumours allege he was poisoned by Khorloogiin Choibalsan.
1932 armed uprising in Mongolia: The failure of collectivization led to widespread uprisings and a temporary thaw.
Prince Demchugdongrub formed the Mongol Military Government, a non-Communist state independent from China, in Inner Mongolia.
The Mongol Military Government was renamed the Mongol United Autonomous Government.
Stalinist purges in Mongolia: The terror ended.
Battle of Khalkhyn Gol: The battle ended in a Japanese defeat. A truce was negotiated between Japan and the Soviet Union.
The Mongol United Autonomous Government was renamed the Mongolian Autonomous Federation, or Mengjiang.

The Republic of China requested Soviet help in the war against Japan, and offered recognition of the independence of Outer Mongolia in exchange according to the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance.
The Chinese government recognized the independence of Mongolian People's Republic.
The newly established People's Republic of China recognized Mongolia and agreed to establish diplomatic relations.
Herds were successfully collectivized.
The Republic of China (ROC) on Taiwan renounced the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance.
The ROC blocked the accession of the Mongolian People's Republic's entry to the United Nations.
Mongolia became a member of the Comecon.
Sino-Soviet split: The MPRP leadership sided with the Soviet Union in a falling-out with China.
Yumjaagiin Tsedenbal purged the intelligentsia.
Sino-Soviet split: The Soviet Union stationed a large army on Mongolian territory in response to threats of Chinese aggression.
Tsedenbal was ousted from all positions by the Politburo.
Mongolia established diplomatic relations with the United States.
Large-scale pro-democracy demonstrations were held in sub-zero weather.
Mongolia and the Soviet Union announced that all Soviet troops would be withdrawn from Mongolia by 1992.
The MDU launched a mass hunger strike demanding the resignation of Jambyn Batmönkh and the Politburo.
The Politburo of the Central Committee of the MPRP and Batmönkh announced their resignation.

The first democratically elected People's Great Khural took office; the office of the President of the Mongolian People's Republic was created with then-chairman of the presidium Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat as its first officeholder.

The first session of the newly established State Little Khural, the lower house of the People's Great Khural, was convened with 50 members. The office of the Vice President of the Mongolian People's Republic was created with Little Khural chairman Radnaasümbereliin Gonchigdorj as its first and only officeholder.
A new election law was passed.
An election was held for the first unicameral legislature, the State Great Khural. The MPRP won a supermajority of 60 seats.
The State Little Khural and the office of the Vice President was dissolved as the first session of the State Great Khural convened.
The opposition Democratic Union Coalition (DUC) won the 1996 parliamentary election. Subsequently, the first non-Communist government was elected into office.
Mendsaikhany Enkhsaikhan became the first Democratic prime minister.
MPRP candidate Natsagiin Bagabandi defeated incumbent president and DUC candidate Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat in the 1997 presidential election.
Prime Minister Enkhsaikhan was forced to resign due to internal party pressure.
DUC chairman Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj was elected (61–6) to succeed Enkhsaikhan.
Sanjaasürengiin Zorig, Minister of Infrastructure and one of the Democratic leaders of the 1990 revolution, was murdered in his home.
Janlavyn Narantsatsralt was nominated by the State Great Khural and accepted by president Bagabandi as the next prime minister.

Prime Minister Narantsatsralt was forced to resign after a controversial letter to the Russian Federation. Rinchinnyamyn Amarjargal was nominated to succeed Narantsatsralt and served until the 2000 election.

The MPRP won 72 out of 76 seats in the State Great Khural; a new government was formed by Prime Minister and MPRP chairman Nambaryn Enkhbayar. The DUC witnessed a major electoral wipeout, winning only a single seat.
The Democratic Party of Mongolia was founded after the merger of five former member parties of the now-dissolved DUC.
Incumbent Bagabandi was re-elected as the 2nd President of Mongolia in the 2001 presidential election.
Mongolian troops begin taking part in peace keeping operations in Afghanistan, Iraq and Sudan.
An election resulted in a draw. A coalition was formed between the MPRP and other parties which was headed by Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj.
The governing coalition was dissolved by the MPRP.
A new coalition between the MPRP and smaller parties and defectors was formed under Miyeegombyn Enkhbold.
The governing coalition was led by the MPRP and replaced by a coalition headed by Sanjiin Bayar.
Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj from the Democratic Party was selected 3rd President of Mongolia.
Sanjaagiin Bayar resigned from Primer Ministership due to declining health conditions and was replaced with Sükhbaataryn Batbold.
MPRP restored its 1921 name, Mongolian People's Party (MPP), during its 26th Party Congress.
After the 2012 parliamentary election, a coalition headed by Norovyn Altankhuyag from Democratic party was formed.
Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj from Democratic Party, was re-elected in the 2013 presidential election.
Altankhuyag lost a motion of no confidence (36–30), thereby resigned as prime minister and Democratic party chairman
Chimediin Saikhanbileg succeeded Altankhuyag as next prime minister, Zandaakhüügiin Enkhbold succeeded as Democratic party chairman
In the 2016 parliamentary election, the MPP won a supermajority of 65 seats in the State Great Khural.

Party chairman Miyeegombyn Enkhbold was elected the next chairman of the State Great Khural, whilst Jargaltulgyn Erdenebat was appointed as the next prime minister during the first parliamentary session.
During the 2017 presidential election
Erdenebat was voted out of office for alleged incompetence and corruption.
Deputy Prime Minister Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh was nominated and appointed as Erdenebat's successor.
Khürelsükh succeeded speaker Enkhbold as the next MPP chairman.
Gautama Buddha is born in Kapilvastu in 563 BCE (died in 483 BCE) in Lumbini (present-day Nepal).
Establishment of the Soma dynasty.
Shivadeva I becomes the king.
Following the death of Amshuverma, Uday Deva becomes the king reviving the Licchavi dynasty's rule.
Uday Deva is ousted by his brother Dhruva Deva, and Jishnu Gupta. He goes to Tibet for help. Dhruva Deva and Jishnu Gupta rule together.
Bishnu Gupta, son of Jishnu Gupta, and Bhimarjuna Deva rule together.
Shivadeva II, the son of Narendradeva, starts his reign. He marries Batsa Devi, daughter of the prince Bhogvarma of Magadha.
King Nanyadeva of the Karnat dynasty dies. He is succeeded by his son Gangadeva.
King Arimalla is succeeded by his son Abhaya Malla.
Doya from Mithila (Karnat dynasty) invades Nepal three times within two years.
A period of political struggle begins between the House of Bhonta (the region of Banepa) headed by Jayabhimadeva and the House of Tripura (Bhadgaon) headed by Jayasimha Malla.
King Jayadeva Malla dies. The two contending houses reach an agreement to share the throne alternately. Jayabhimadeva becomes the King following the agreement.
Jayasimha Malla becomes the King following the agreement between the two Houses.
King Jayasimha Malla is deposed with the help of House of Bhonta; Ananta Malla becomes the king.
Jitari Malla of the Khasa area in the Karnali region attacks Nepal three times until 1290.
Doya from Mithila invades Nepal again penetrating as far as Bhadgaon, and inflicting fines on the House of Tripura.
King Ananta Malla dies, leaving the throne vacant.

After Jayasaktideva of House of Bhonta is defeated by Jayatunga Malla of House of Tripura, Jayasaktideva calls the Doya for help. This backfires as the Doya imprisoned Brahmins, looted people and set houses on fire.
Following an agreement between the House of Tripura and the Tirhuts, along with other wealth, Devalakshmidevi, the daughter of Jayatunga Malla, is given in marriage to King Harisimhadeva.
Ripu Malla from the Khasa kingdom visits the Kathmandu valley.
Jayarudra Malla, the son of Jayatunga Malla, controls much of the valley.
After five years without a King, Jayarudra Malla installs Jayanandadeva, his rival from the House of Bhonta, as the ruler.
Jayarudra Malla withdraws support for Jayanandadeva and installs Jayari Malla, his relative and the son of Ananta Malla, as the King.
The Karnat Kingdom of Mithila is annexed by the King of Delhi. The invader then sets up a vassal state appointing from the Oiniwar dynasty a ruler of the region.

King Harisimhadeva of Mithila, along with his wife Devalakshmidevi and so Jagatsimha flees to Kathmandu Valley. Harisimha dies on the way and Devalakshmidevi, and Jagatsimha were welcomed by her brother, Jayarudra Malla.
Aditya Malla from the Khasa Kingdom invades the Kathmandu valley.
Jayarudra Malla dies at the age of 30, leaving Nayakadevi, his daughter, to assume the throne of House of Tripura.
Harischandra, the husband of Nayakadevi, was poisoned by the nobles.
King Jayari Malla dies.
Rajalladevi is born to Nayakadevi and Jagatsimha. Nayakadevi dies ten days later and Jagatsimha was thrown to prison leaving Rajalladevi to the care of Devalakshmidevi.

Devalakshmidevi comes to an agreement with the House of Bhonta on the condition that a king would be from the House of Bhonta while Devalakshmidevi would act as the de facto ruler. Following this agreement, Jayarajadeva, the illegitimate son of the late King Jayanandadeva, becomes the King. Devalakshmidevi, however, is given royal titles higher than the King himself.
Rajalladevi marries Jayasthiti Malla. It is generally accepted that Jayasthiti Malla was brought from Mithila by Devalakshmidevi to marry Rajalladevi.
King Jayarajadeva dies. He is succeeded by his son Jayarjunadeva.
Devalakshmidevi dies. Jayasthiti Malla starts on gathering political power.
King Jayasthiti Malla dies. His three sons Dharma Malla, Jyoti Malla, and Kiti Malla rule together.
Jyoti Malla rules as the sole king of Kathmandu Valley after the death of both his brothers.
King Jyoti Malla dies. His son Yakshya Malla succeeds him.
King Ratna Malla dies. His son Surya Malla succeeds him as the king.
Mukunda Sen of Palpa attacks the entire Kathmandu valley and surrounds both Kantipur, and Patan. He is defeated by the combined forces of the valley.
King Surya Malla dies. He is succeeded by his son Amara Malla. Amara Malla annexed several villages north-west of Kantipur.
King Amara Malla dies. His son Mahendra Malla succeeds him. Mahendra Malla issued the first silver coins.
King Mahendra Malla is succeeded by his first son Sadashiva Malla.
Shivasimha Malla, the second son of Mahendra Malla, deposes his brother Sadashiva Malla and rules Kantipur. Sadashiva takes refuge in Bhadgaon where he dies.
King Shivasimha Malla annexes Patan and installs his son Harisimhadeva as the governor. Harisimhadeva dies shortly afterwards, and his son Siddhi Narasimha Malla succeeds him as the governor.
King Shivasimha Malla dies. His son Lakshmi Narasimha Malla succeeds him as the King of Kantipur, and his grandson Siddhi Narasimha Malla declares Patan independent from Kantipur.
King Lakshmi Narasimha Malla goes insane after executing his loyal minister. Pratap Malla imprisons him and rules Kantipur.
Nripendra Malla starts his reign after his Pratap Malla's death defying the wishes of his father to install Mahipatendra Malla as the king.
Parthibendra Malla, another son of Pratap Malla, starts his reign after the death of King Nripendra Malla.

King Parthibendra Malla is poisoned by the nobles and on his death, as many as twenty-four women went Sati. He is succeeded by his 14 years old son Bhupalendra Malla with his wife Riddhilakshmi acting as the regent.
Lakshminarayan, a minister, rises to the power of supreme authority and inscribes his name on the coin issued by the monarch. He also assassinates prominent nobles.
Lakshminarayan is assassinated following a rumor of illicit relationship with the regent and the king's mother, Riddhilakshmi.
King Bhupalendra Malla dies. He is succeeded by his son Bhaskara Malla.
King Bhaskara Malla proclaims the title of King of Patan and issues coins under the name Gajapati Mahindra Simha.

After about six months in confinement to be safe from the plague, King Bhaskara Malla returns to the palace after the death rate dropped. He dies some days later due to the plague. He is succeeded by Jagajjaya Malla, the grandson of Mahipatendra Malla.
King Jagajjaya Malla's first son Rajendra Malla dies.
Jayaprakash Malla succeeds King Jagajjaya Malla after the latter's death.
British East India Company gains control of Bengal.
Conquest of Chaudandi and Majh Kirant states.
Bhimsen Thapa falls, beginning unstable period in court politics.
War starts with China (until 1858).
Jang Bahadur receives the title of Rana.
Prime minister Jung Bahadur Rana dies; Ranodip Singh Kunwar becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Ranodip Singh Kunwar is assassinated by his nephews; Bir Shumsher becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Bir Shumsher dies; Dev Shumsher becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Dev Shumsher is deposed by his relatives; Chandra Shumsher becomes the prime minister.

Nepali National Congress is formed (led by BP Koirala, Matrika Prasad Koirala, Ganesh Man Singh, etc.).

Matrika Prasad Koirala becomes the first commoner to be elected a prime minister
King Tribhuwan dies, King Mahendra ascends throne.
New constitution provides for non-party system of councils known as Panchayat under which king exercises sole power. First elections to Rastrya Panchayat held in 1963.
King Mahendra dies, succeeded by Birendra.
Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist–Leninist) begins civil disobedience campaign for restoration of multi-party system.
Trade and transit dispute with India leads to border blockade by Delhi resulting in worsening economic situation.

Second multi-party election is held. CPN (UML) led by Man Mohan Adhikari wins the election with 88 votes. NC led by Girija Prasad Koirala wins 83 votes. RPP led by Surya Bahadur Thapa wins 20 votes. Man Mohan Adhikari heads a minority government.
Prime minister Man Mohan Adhikari resigns after losing in a Congress-led no-confidence motion. Sher Bahadur Deuba becomes the new prime minister.
Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba loses a no-confidence vote, ushering in a period of increased political instability, with frequent changes of the prime minister.
Girija Prasad Koirala returns as the prime minister, heading the ninth government in 10 years.
Maoist rebels step up campaign of violence. Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala quits over the violence; succeeded by Sher Bahadur Deuba.
Maoists end four-month-old truce with government, declare peace talks with government failed. Launch coordinated attacks on army and police posts.
The government declares a state of emergency throughout the country and full mobilization of the army against rebels listing the CPN (Maoist Centre) as a "terrorist organization".
King Gyanendra dissolves the parliament and called for early elections. Sher Bahadur Deuba heads the interim government, and renews the state of emergency.

Prime minister Deuba formally asks the king to defer the election dates until November 2003. King Gyanendra responds by dismissing the government headed by Deuba, removing Deuba as the prime minister, postponing the elections indefinitely, and assuming full executive power.
Lokendra Bahadur Chand is appointed as the prime minister.
Rebels, government declare ceasefire.
Lokendra Bahadur Chand resigns as PM; king appoints his own nominee Surya Bahadur Thapa as new premier (to June).
Rebels pull out of peace talks with government and end seven-month truce. The following months see resurgence of violence and frequent clashes between students/activists and police.
Nepal joins the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Royalist Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa resigns following weeks of street protests by opposition groups.
King Gyanendra reappoints Sher Bahadur Deuba as prime minister with the task of holding elections.
King lifts the state of emergency amid international pressure.
Several political parties and the CPN (Maoist Centre) sign an agreement to work together against the rule of King Gyanendra.
Parliament votes unanimously to curtail the king's political powers. The government and Maoist rebels begin peace talks, the first in nearly three years.
Rebel leader Chairman Prachanda and PM Koirala hold talks – the first such meeting between the two sides – and agree that the Maoists should be brought into an interim government.
Maoist leaders enter parliament under the terms of a temporary constitution. Violent ethnic protests erupt in the south-east; demonstrators demand autonomy for the region.
Former Maoist rebels join interim government, a move that takes them into the political mainstream.
Elections for a constituent assembly pushed back to November.
A US offer to resettle thousands of Bhutanese refugees in Nepal has raised hopes but has also sparked tension in the camps, says Human Rights Watch.
Three bombs hit Kathmandu in the first attack in the capital since the end of the Maoist insurgency.
Maoists quit interim government to press demand for monarchy to be scrapped. This forces the postponement of November's constituent assembly elections.
UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon urges Nepal's parties to sink their differences to save the peace process.
Parliament approves abolition of monarchy as part of peace deal with Maoists, who agree to re-join government.
A series of bomb blasts kill and injure dozens in the southern Terai plains. Groups there have been demanding regional autonomy.
Nepali Congress leader Bal Chandra Poudel attacked by maoists in Dandagaun, Rasuwa during election

The First Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the CPN (MC) emerged victorious winning 220 out of the 575 seats. It forms the government with seven other communist parties including the CPN (UML).
Maoist ministers resign from the cabinet in a row over who should be the next head of state.
Prachanda is elected as the prime minister by the constituent assembly.

Prime minister Prachanda sacks General Rookmangud Katawal. CPN (UML) withdraws its support from the government in protest. President Ram Baran Yadav overrides the decision resulting in the resignation of Prachanda the next day.
Madhav Kumar Nepal of CPN (UML) becomes the prime minister with support from 22 of the 25 parties.
Former prime minister and NCP leader Girija Prasad Koirala dies.
Prime minister Madhav Kumar Nepal announces his resignation blaming the CPN (MC) for their continuous obstruction in the government.

CPN (MC) withdraws its candidate and backs Jhala Nath Khanal of CPN (UML). Khanal becomes the prime minister after more than seven months of political gridlock and more than sixteen rounds of voting in the parliament.
Dr. Baburam Bhattarai is elected as the prime minister after he gets support from some smaller parties after the resignation of Jhala Nath Khanal.
Prime minister Baburam Bhattarai dissolves the constituent assembly after it failed to promulgate a new constitution four years after its election and calls for a fresh election for 22 November.

Prime minister Baburam Bhattarai resigns. Chief Justice Khil Raj Regmi becomes the interim prime minister until the elections after four main political parties agreed to form a CJ-led electoral cabinet.

The Second Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the NC led by Sushil Koirala emerges as the largest party winning 196 out of the 576 seats. The CPN (UML) wins 175 seats while the CPN (MC) wins 80 seats.
Sushil Koirala of Nepali Congress is elected as the prime minister with CPN (UML) backing.
CPN (UML) leader KP Sharma Oli is elected as the prime minister by the parliament with the backing from CPN (MC).
Nepal holds its first general election since the end of the civil war, with the Communist party's alliance winning.
The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacts Nepal.
Prime Minister Khadga Prasad Sharma Oli was replaced by Sher Bahadur Deuba following a constitutional crisis within the government.
The population of Nepal reached 30.2 million people.
2026 Nepal–Tibet floods

The archaeological site of Riwat 55 dates back to this period. It is modern form of Early Riwat Site. Riwat 55 contains a structure that includes a low wall footing, a pit, and a stone-lined niche, all associated with a freshly flaked stone assemblage that included blades.

Mature phases of the Indus Valley Civilization begins. The civilization used an early form of the Indus signs, also called Indus script. Over the course of next 1000–1500 years, inhabitants of the civilization developed new techniques in handicraft (carnelian products and seal carving) and metallurgy (copper, bronze, lead, and tin) had elaborate urban planning, baked brick houses, efficient drainage systems, water supply systems, and clusters of large non-residential buildings. The civilization depended significantly on trade, was the first civilization to use wheeled transport in form of bullock carts, and also used boats.

The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro become large metropolises and the civilization expands to over 2,500 cities and settlements across the whole region of modern-day Pakistan, covering a region of around one million square miles, which was larger than the land area of its contemporaries Egypt and Mesopotamia combined, and also had superior urban planning and sewage systems. The civilization began using the mature Indus script for its writing system.

The culture, artichetere, technology and educational system of Indus Valley civilization reached at its zenith with Harappa and Kot Diji as main centres. These fluctuations reflect complex and dynamic political, ideological, and economic processes that are an integral part of urban society.
Late Harappan Phase (Cemetery H Culture)

Middle and Late Vedic period (to 500 BCE)
Iron Age of Indian subcontinent (including today's Pakistan)
Vedic period ends.

Persian rule is at its zenith.
Roruka as capital of Sauvira Kingdom become most important trading center of Indian subcontinent, also mentioned in early Buddhist literature.
Persian rule in the Pakistan ends after Darius III is defeated by Alexander the Great, who establishes the Macedonian Empire after inheriting the Persian Achaemenid Empire.
Porus who ruled parts of the Punjab, fought Alexander at the Battle of the Hydaspes River.
During the Mallian Campaign, Alexander was seriously wounded by an arrow in the chest and this became reason of his death.
Mauryan Empire is founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
Chandragupta Maurya defeats Seleucus Nicator of the Seleucid Empire.
Seleucus gives up his territories (Balochistan) to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 elephants. Seleucus offers his daughter in marriage to Chandragupta to seal their friendship.
Arrival of Scythians (Sakas) from Central Asia.
Indo-Parthian Kingdom was established and conquered present northern Pakistan.
Sri Gupta starts the establishment of Gupta Empire in Indian subcontinent (including present Pakistan).
Kushans decline and are dominated by Indo-Sassanians.
Chandragupta I ascends the throne of Gupta Empire.
Kidarite Kingdom came to power in the region of modern-day Pakistan.
Collapse of Gupta Empire after the death of Skandagupta.
Sassanians and Turks overthrow Huns.
Rai dynasty reached at its zenith and covered whole of Pakistan and Afghanistan with the capital of Aror, Sindh.
Islam arrived in Indian subcontinent. Rashidun Caliphate defeated Rai dynasty in the Battle of Rasil and Balochistan become easternmost frontier of Rashidun Caliphate.
Turk Shahi gained control west of the Indus River, including Gandhara.
At the death of Chach of Alor, the Brahmin dynasty reached its zenith and he was succeeded by his brother Chandar of Sindh.
Chandar of Sindh died and succeeded by his nephew Raja Dahir, last Hindu Maharaja of Sindh.
Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf sent a force under Ubaidullah ibn Nabhan to raid Debal. Ubaidullah was defeated and slain in battle.

Al-Hajjaj dispatched a second, larger force under Budail ibn Tahafe towards Debal. Budail’s army met the forces of Jaisiah (son of Raja Dahir) in a day-long battle. The Umayyad army was routed, and Budail was killed.
Muhammad Bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and established Umayyad Islamic rule on Sindh and southern Punjab (Multan) on the orders of Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf.

Umayyad Era finished and Abbasid Era begins. Mansur ibn Jumhur al-Kalbi revolted against Umayyad Dynasty during Abbasid Revolution and after Abbasid victory in revolution, he was confirmed as Abbasid Governor of Sindh.
Dynastic rule of Habbaris over Sindh begin under suzerainty of Abbasid Caliphate.
Hindu Shahis captured Kingdom of Kabul Shahi and expanded their rule in Khyber Pukhtunkhwa and Punjab.
Habbari dynasty rule expanded over whole of Sindh, Southern Balochistan and southern Punjab (Multan).
Sabuktigin of Ghaznavid dynasty defeated many times Hindu Shahi ruler Jayapala and became ruler of domains east of the Indus River.
Mahmud Ghazni defeated Raja Jayapala of Hindu Shahi; after that Jayapala commits suicide.

Mahmud Ghazni defeats Raja Tarnochalpal and Punjab becomes part of Ghaznavid dynasty. In this way whole of Pakistan comes under Muslim rule; Punjab and Khyber Pukhtunkhwa under Ghaznavid Empire, Sindh under Habbari dynasty while Makran (Balochistan) under Caliphate.
Alberuni arrives in Indian subcontinent; death of Mahmud Ghazni.
Muhammad of Ghurid dynasty defeats Qarmatians rulers of Multan in 1175.
Muhammad Ghori along with Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad ends the rule of Ghaznavid dynasty after having captured Lahore.
"Victory of Prithviraj Chauhan". First Battle of Tarain fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj III. Ghori is defeated by Prithivi Raj Chauhan III.
"Victory of Muhammad Ghori". Second Battle of Tarain fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithivi Raj Chauhan III. Chauhan is defeated by Muhammad Ghori.
Qutb al-Din Aibak becomes deputy of Ghurid Empire in Indian subcontinent.
Khukhrains kill Muhammad Ghori during a raid on his camp on the Jhelum River.
End of Ghurid Era.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak establishes Delhi Sultanate by becoming first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate from Mamluk dynasty.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak died while playing polo.
Aram Shah becomes new Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Shams ud-Din Iltutmish defeats Aram Shah in the Battle of Delhi and become third Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Genghis Khan invades Punjab during rule of Iltutmish.
Iltutmish dies and Rukn ud din Firuz become fourth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Razia Sultana abolishes the rule of Rukn ud din Firuz and become fifth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Muiz ud din Bahram becomes sixth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Murder of Razia Sultan by nobles of Chalisa.
Murder of Muiz ud din Bahram by army. Ala ud din Masud becomes seventh Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Nasiruddin Mahmud becomes eighth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate with the support of Corps of Forty. Balban rules on the behave of Nasiruddin Mahmud as a deputy of empire.
Nasiruddin Mahmud dies without any hier. Ghiyas ud din Balban becomes ninth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Delhi Sultanate decisively defeats the army of Mongol Empire at the battle of Beas River.
Muiz ud din Qaiqabad becomes tenth Sultan of Delhi Sultanate after the death of his grandfather Ghiyas ud din Balban.
Murder of Muiz ud din Qaiqabad by Jalaluddin Firuz Khalji, an army commander. Shamsuddin Kayumars becomes eleventh Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Jalaluddin Firuz Khalji ends the Mamluk Dynasty by murdering Shamsuddin Kayumars. Establishment of Khalji dynasty. Jalaluddin becomes twelfth Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Alauddin Khalji murders Jalaluddin Firuz Khalji and become thirteen Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
Allauddin Khalji conquers Multan and eliminates all surviving members of his predecessor Jalaluddin Firuz Khalji.
Mongol Army invades Punjab and Sindh but Delhi Sultanate decisively defeats them and crushes away from Pakistan.
Mongols once again invades Sindh and occupies fort of Sivistan but Delhi Sultanate decisively defeats them.
Alauddin Khalji died due to severe illness.
Shihabuddin Omar succeeded Alauddin Khalji with the help of Malik Kafur and becomes the 14th Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
After the assassination of Malik Kafur, Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah dethroned his brother Shihabuddin Omar and himself becomes 15th Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.

At the Dhaka session of the ruling Muslim League party, prime minister Khawaja Nazimuddin declares Urdu the national language of the state of Pakistan.

Mehar Dil Khan Khattak, commander in chief of Pashtunistan armed forces, surrendered to the Pakistani authorities.

Gen Muhammad Ayub Khan's term as the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army extended by PM Feroz Khan Noon on request of President Mirza
Presidential rule imposed in East Pakistan

August: Second Balochistan conflict begins when the palace guards of Ahmad of Kalat attack deputy commissioner. It is followed by Pakistan army's bombardment and assault on Kalat palace and arrest of Ahmad of Kalat. Protests against the government break out in Balochistan.

1958 East Pakistan-India Border Clashes, Armed skirmishes between East Pakistan and India took place between troops of the East Pakistan Rifles (EPR) and the Indian Army in the small village of Lakshmipur, located in Sylhet District
All powers of Ahmad of Kalat are stripped off and he is jailed in Lahore.

Ayub and his Cabinet takes oaths. In a dramatic turn of events late night, President Iskander Mirza resigned, giving over his office to Gen Ayub Khan. Ayub now becomes the country's 2nd President. Nauroz Khan launches an insurgency against Pakistan government for abolishment of One Unit Scheme and release of Ahmad of Kalat. Battles erupt between militants and Pakistan army.
Iskander Mirza is exiled to London
Gawadar, formerly a feif of the Sultan of Oman, is handed over to Pakistan after its purchase.

18 April: The government takes over dailies The Pakistan Times, Imroze and weekly Lail-o-Nihar.

26 October: Ayub Khan announces his system of 80,000 Basic Democrats, who would further form the electoral college for the elections of the President and the members of the Central and Provisional Legislature.
Dir campaign, a Pakistan backed civilian revolt against the Nawab of Dir is crushed.
Ayub Khan becomes first elected president.
Nauroz Khan and his followers surrender to Pakistani authorities concluding the Second Balochistan conflict.

September: Bajaur Campaign, Afghan troops and irregulars invade Bajaur district but they are repulsed by Pakistani tribesmen and airforce.
September: Dir campaign, Afghan troops and irregulars enter into Dir to support Nawab of Dir against a Pakistan backed revolt. Afghan forces are repulsed and 200 soldiers of Nawab are killed.

31 October: A cyclone more powerful than that which hit on 10 October sweeps across East Pakistan, killing 14,174 people.
October: Dir campaign, Pakistani special forces carry out a coup against Nawab Jahan khan of Dir, he is arrested and exiled. A constitutional government is established.
Constitution Commission, appointed by President Ayub Khan, presents its report, specifying pinpoints the failures of parliamentary government in Pakistan.
April: Elections for the National and provincial assembly were held on the basis of Basic Democracies.
July: the National Assembly passes the Political Parties Act, legalizing the formation of political parties.
Start of Third Balochistan conflict by Baloch militants to persuade the government to share revenue form Sui gas fields with the tribal leaders and lifting of One Unit Scheme.
2 January: Fatima Jinnah lost the presidential elections, Ayub completes the second term.

Prince Vijaya had his followers landed at a place called Supparaka; the women landed at a place called Mahiladipaka, and the children landed at a place called Naggadipa. Vijaya's ship later reached Sri Lanka, on the North west coast of present-day Puttalam, on the day of the Parinibbaana of The Buddha.

During the reign of Vijaya, in addition to Tambapaṇṇī, the King and his ministers founded settlements like Anuraadhagaama, Upatissagāma, Ujjeni, Uruvelaa and Vijithapura located along the river banks of the Malwathu Oya and the Kala Oya in the northwestern region of Sri Lanka.
Prince Vijaya dies without a legitimate successor after a reign of 38 years. Upatissa, chief minister of Vijaya, becomes regent while a successor is brought over from Sinhapura.
The nephew of Prince Vijaya, Panduvasdeva, succeeds him to the throne. He arrives one year after the death of Vijaya and brings with him 32 sons of ministers.
Death of Panduvasdeva after a reign of 30 years. Abhaya, eldest son of Panduvasdeva, ascends the throne.
Deposition of Abhaya after a reign of 20 years; Prince Tissa, younger brother of Abhaya, becomes regent.

Prince Tissa was not acknowledged universally as the Sinhalese king, remained as regent during the Nineteen Years' War (458–439 BC), which ended with the Battle of Labugamaka where with the aid of the Yakkhas and others, Pandukabhaya slew eight of his uncles who were against him.
Pandukabhaya, nephew of Abhaya and Tissa, takes the capital Upatissagāma and is crowned the new Sinhalese king.
Abhaya Wewa built
Death of Pandukabhaya after a reign of 70 years. Mutasiva, son of Pandukabhaya, ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over northern Sri Lanka (Jaffna Peninsula).
Total solar eclipse visible over southeastern Sri Lanka.
Total solar eclipse visible across almost the entirety of Sri Lanka.
Death of Mutasiva after a reign of 60 years. Devanampiya Tissa, second son of Mutasiva, ascends the throne.
Death of Devanampiya Tissa after a reign of 40 years. Uttiya, younger brother of Devanampiya Tissa, ascends the throne.
Mahinda Thero passes away at the age of 80 in the eighth year of the reign of Uttiya.
Sanghamitta Therii passes away at the age of 79 in the ninth year of the reign of Uttiya.
Death of Uttiya after a reign of 10 years. Mahasiva, younger brother of Uttiya, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahasiva after a reign of 10 years. Suratissa, younger brother of Mahasiva, ascends the throne.
Suratissa is slain in battle after a reign of 10 years; South Indian invaders Sena and Guttika usurp the throne.
Asela, son of Mutasiva, overthrows Sena and Guttika in battle after a reign of 22 years reclaiming the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible across Sri Lanka except the far northern region, during the reign of King Dutugamunu.
Death of Dutugemunu after a reign of 24 years. Saddha Tissa, younger brother of Dutugemunu, ascends the throne.
Saddha Tissa dies and is succeeded by his younger son Thulatthana, whose ascension was endorsed and supported as a result of the decision made by royal advisors and Buddhist monks.

Death of Saddha Tissa after a reign of 18 years. Thulatthana, second son of Saddha Tissa, ascends the throne, but is deposed and killed after a reign of 1 month and 10 days; Lanjatissa, elder brother of Thulatthana, ascends the throne.
One month and ten days after his ascension, Lanja Tissa usurps his younger brother Thulatthana and takes the throne upon hear of his succession.
Death of Lanjatissa after a reign of 9 years and 15 days. Khallata Naga, younger brother of Lanjatissa, ascends the throne.

Khallata Naga is assassinated by his own commander-in-chief, Kammaharattaka. However, Kammaharattaka's rule last only a day and is killed by Prince Vattagamini, the youngest brother of Khallata Naga. Prince Vattagamini ascends the throne as Valagamba.

Only five months into his regin Valagamba faced internal threats from a Brahman named Tiya (or Tissa) from Ruhuna, South Lanka and external threats from Tamil forces from South India. The Tamil army vanquished Tiya and defeated Valagamba in battle forcing him to flee into exile for fourteen years. Pulahatha, the first of the The Five Dravidians seized and ruled the Sinhalese throne.

The fourteen years of rule of The Five Dravidians was disastrous for the country and its institutions. The Beminitiya Seya, an unprecedented famine during that period caused the rapid decline of Buddhism in the country with many thousands of monks and laymen dying of starvation.
Pulahatha is slain after a reign of 3 years; Bahiya ascends the throne.
Bahiya is slain after a reign of 2 years; Panaya Mara ascends the throne.
Panaya Mara is slain after a reign of 7 years; Pilaya Mara ascends the throne.
Pilaya Mara is slain after a reign of 7 months; Dathika ascends the throne.
After building and army during his 14 years in exile Valagamba launches a successful attack on Dathika, the last of the Five Dravidians defeating him and taking back control of the country.
Death of Valagamba after a second reign of 12 years. Mahakuli Mahatissa, nephew and adopted son of Valagamba (son of Khallata Naga), ascends the throne.
Death of Mahakuli Mahatissa after a reign of 14 years. Chora Naga, son of Valagamba, ascends the throne.
Chora Naga is poisoned after a reign of 12 years. Kuda Tissa, son of Mahakuli Mahatissa, ascends the throne.
Kuda Tissa is poisoned by Queen Anula after a reign of 3 years; Anula, widow of Chora Naga and Kuda Tissa, rules as queen regnant.
Anula is executed after a reign of 5 years; Kutakanna Tissa, second son of Mahakuli Mahatissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Kutakanna Tissa after a reign of 22 years. Bhatika Abhaya, son of Kutakanna Tissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Bhatika Abhaya after a reign of 28 years. Mahadathika Mahanaga, younger brother of Bhatikabhaya Tissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahadathika Mahanaga after a reign of 12 years. Amandagamani Abhaya, son of Mahadathika Mahanaga, ascends the throne.
Amandagamani Abhaya is assassinated after a reign of 9 years and 8 months; Kanirajanu Tissa, younger brother of Amandagamani Abhaya, ascends the throne.
Death of Kaniraja Tissa after a reign of 3 years. Chulabhaya, son of Amandagamani Abhaya, ascends the throne.
Death of Chulabhaya after a reign of 1 year. Sivali, sister of Chulabhaya, rules as queen regnant, but is deposed after 4 months; Ilanaga, nephew of Chulabhaya and Sivali, ascends the throne.
Annius Plocamus, a Roman tax collector, visits Sri Lanka during the reign of Claudius.
Death of Ilanaga after a reign of 9 years. Chandamukha, son of Ilanaga, ascends the throne.
Chandamukha is killed after a reign of 8 years and 8 months; Yassalalaka Tissa, younger brother of Chandamukha Siva, ascends the throne.
Yassalalaka Tissa is slain after a reign of 7 years and 8 months; Subharaja (Subha), royal gatekeeper, usurps the throne.
Subharaja is slain after a reign of 6 years; Vasabha, member of the Lambakanna clan, ascends the throne, founding the First Lambakanna Dynasty.
Death of Vasabha after a reign of 44 years. Vankanasika Tissa, son of Vasabha, ascends the throne.
Death of Vankanasika Tissa after a reign of 3 years.
Gajabahu I, son of Vankanasika Tissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Gajabahu I after a reign of 22 years. Mahallaka Naga, father-in-law of Gajabahu I, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahallaka Naga after a reign of 6 years. Bhatika Tissa, son of Mahallaka Naga, ascends the throne.
Construction of monumental architecture.
Death of Bhatika Tissa after a reign of 24 years. Kanittha Tissa, younger brother of Bhatika Tissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Kanittha Tissa after a reign of 18 years. Khujjanaga, son of Kanittha Tissa, ascends the throne.
Khujjanaga is murdered after a reign of 2 years; Kunchanaga, younger brother of Khujjanaga, ascends the throne.
Kunchanaga is deposed after a reign of 1 year; Siri Naga I, brother-in-law of Kunchanaga, ascends the throne.
Death of Siri Naga I after a reign of 19 years. Voharika Tissa, son of Siri Naga I, ascends the throne.
Voharika Tissa is overthrown and killed after a reign of 22 years; Abhaya Naga, younger brother of Voharika Tissa, ascends the throne.
Death of Abhaya Naga after a reign of 8 years. Siri Naga II, nephew of Abhaya Naga (son of Voharika Tissa), ascends the throne.
Death of Siri Naga II after a reign of 2 years. Vijaya Kumara, son of Sirinaga II, ascends the throne.
Vijaya Kumara is slain after a reign of 1 year; Sangha Tissa I, noble of the Lambakanna clan, ascends the throne.
Sangha Tissa I is poisoned after a reign of 4 years; Siri Sangha Bodhi I, noble of the Lambakanna clan, ascends the throne.
Siri Sangha Bodhi I abdicates after a reign of 4 years; Gothabhaya, chief minister and Lambakanna noble, ascends the throne.
Death of Gothabhaya after a reign of 13 years. Jettha Tissa I, elder son of Gothabhaya, ascends the throne.
Death of Jettha Tissa I after a reign of 14 years. Mahasena, younger brother of Jettha Tissa I, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahasena after a reign of 27 years. Sirimeghavanna, son of Mahasena, ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over southeastern Sri Lanka during the Anuradhapura period.
Death of Sirimeghavanna after a reign of 27 years. Jettha Tissa II, younger brother of Sirimeghavanna, ascends the throne.
Death of Jettha Tissa II after a reign of 9 years. Buddhadasa, son of Jettha Tissa II, ascends the throne.
Death of Buddhadasa after a reign of 28 years. Upatissa I, eldest son of Buddhadasa, ascends the throne.
Upatissa I is murdered after a reign of 41 years; Mahanama, younger brother of Upatissa I, ascends the throne.
Dhammapala composes commentaries on remaining portions of the Canon (such as the Udana, Itivuttaka, Theragatha, and Therigatha) along with extensive sub-commentaries.
Death of Mahanama after a reign of 22 years. Soththisena, son of Mahanama, ascends the throne and dies after a reign of 1 day; Chattagahaka Jantu, husband of Mahanama's daughter, ascends the throne.

Death of Chattagahaka Jantu after a reign of 1 year. Mittasena, an outsider of unknown royal lineage, ascends the throne and is slain after a reign of 1 year by Pandyan invaders; Pandu captures the throne.
Bhikkhuni Devasara leads a delegation of Sri Lankan nuns to China, carrying a sapling of the Bodhi tree to help establish the Bhikkhuni ordination line.
Death of Pandu after a reign of 5 years; Parinda, son of Pandu, ascends the throne.
Death of Parinda after a reign of 3 years; Khudda Parinda, younger brother of Parinda, ascends the throne.
Death of Khudda Parinda after a reign of 16 years; Tiritara ascends the throne and is slain after 2 months; Dathiya ascends the throne.
Dathiya is slain after a reign of 3 years; Pithiya ascends the throne and is slain after 7 months; Dhatusena, member of the Moriya clan, ascends the throne (Moriya Dynasty).
Dhatusena repels Tamil invaders from South India but is later killed by his son Kassapa I.
Dhatusena is murdered after a reign of 17 years; Kashyapa I, non-royal son of Dhatusena, usurps the throne and moves the capital to Sigiriya.
Kashyapa I commits suicide in battle after a reign of 22 years; Moggallana I, royal son of Dhatusena and half-brother of Kashyapa I, ascends the throne.
The Sacred Hair Relic of the Buddha was brought to Sri Lanka during the reign of Moggallana I.
Death of Moggallana I after a reign of 17 years. Kumara Dhatusena, son of Moggallana I, ascends the throne.
Death of Kumara Dhatusena after a reign of 8 years. Kittisena, son of Kumara Dhatusena, ascends the throne.

Kittisena is murdered after a reign of 9 months; Siva II, maternal uncle of Kittisena, ascends the throne and is slain after 25 days; Upatissa II, brother-in-law of Kumara Dhatusena, ascends the throne.
Upatissa II is slain after a reign of 1 year and 6 months; Silakala Ambasamanera, distant relative of the Moriya clan, ascends the throne.

Death of Silakala Ambasamanera after a reign of 13 years. Dathappabhuti, second son of Silakala Ambasamanera, ascends the throne and is slain after 6 months; Jettha Tissa III (Dathaprabhati), younger brother of Dathappabhuti, ascends the throne and is slain after 5 months; Moggallana II, eldest brother of Rathathiyana and Jettha Tissa III, ascends the throne.

Death of Moggallana II after a reign of 20 years. Kittisiri Meghavanna, son of Moggallana II, ascends the throne and is slain after 19 days; Maha Naga, prime minister under Silakala Ambasamanera, ascends the throne.
Death of Maha Naga after a reign of 5 years. Aggabodhi I, maternal nephew and adopted son of Maha Naga, ascends the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi I after a reign of 44 years. Aggabodhi II, nephew and son-in-law of Aggabodhi I, ascends the throne.

Death of Aggabodhi II after a reign of 10 years. Sangha Tissa II, brother and sword-bearer of Aggabodhi II, ascends the throne and is slain after 2 months; Moggallana III, general under Aggabodhi II, ascends the throne.
Moggallana III is slain after a reign of 5 years; Silameghavanna, general under Moggallana III, ascends the throne.

Death of Silameghavanna after a reign of 9 years. Aggabodhi III, son of Silameghavanna, ascends the throne, but is deposed after a first reign of 6 months; Jettha Tissa III, son of Sangha Tissa II, ascends the throne.
Jettha Tissa III commits suicide in battle after a reign of 5 months; Aggabodhi III regains the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi III after a second reign of 10 years. Dathopa Tissa I, general under Jettha Tissa III, ascends the throne.
Death of Dathopa Tissa I after a reign of 11 years. Kassapa II, younger brother of Aggabodhi III, ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over southern Sri Lanka.
Death of Kassapa II after a reign of 9 years. Dappula I, nephew of Silameghavanna and son-in-law of Kassapa II, ascends the throne.
Deposition of Dappula I after a reign of 3 years; Dathopa Tissa II, nephew of Dathopa Tissa I, ascends the throne.
Death of Dathopa Tissa II after a reign of 9 years. Aggabodhi IV, younger brother of Dathopa Tissa II, ascends the throne.

Death of Aggabodhi IV after a reign of 16 years. Unhanagara Hatthadatha, royal prince of Unhanagara lineage, ascends the throne and is slain after 6 months; Manavanna, son of Kassapa II, ascends the throne, founding the Second Lambakanna Dynasty.
Indian Esoteric Buddhist master Vajrabodhi visits Sri Lanka on his journey to China.
Death of Manavanna after a reign of 35 years. Aggabodhi V, eldest son of Manavanna, ascends the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi V after a reign of 6 years. Kassapa III, younger brother of Aggabodhi V, ascends the throne.
Death of Kassapa III after a reign of 7 years. Mahinda I, youngest brother of Aggabodhi V and Kassapa III, rules as regent.
Death of Mahinda I after a regency of 3 years. Aggabodhi VI, son of Kassapa III, ascends the throne.
Amoghavajra, a disciple of Vajrabodhi, visits Sri Lanka to collect esoteric Buddhist scriptures.
Death of Aggabodhi VI after a reign of 40 years. Aggabodhi VII, son of Mahinda I, ascends the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi VII after a reign of 11 years. Mahinda II, son of Aggabodhi VI, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahinda II after a reign of 5 years. Dappula II, son of Mahinda II, ascends the throne.
Death of Dappula II after a reign of 5 years. Mahinda III, son of Dappula II, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahinda III after a reign of 5 years. Aggabodhi VIII, younger brother of Mahinda III, ascends the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi VIII after a reign of 11 years. Dappula III, younger brother of Aggabodhi VIII, ascends the throne.
Death of Dappula III after a reign of 16 years. Aggabodhi IX, son of Dappula II and cousin of Dappula III, ascends the throne.
Death of Aggabodhi IX after a reign of 3 years. Sena I, younger brother of Aggabodhi IX, ascends the throne.
Srimara Srivallabha invades the Anuradhapura kingdom and captures the northern provinces from Sena I.
Persian Muslim traveler Sulaiman al-Tajir visits Sri Lanka and writes accounts of its trade and gems.
Sena II starts construction on the Mihintale Hospital Complex, considered one of the oldest hospital ruins in the world and the oldest existing hospital ruins in Sri Lanka.
Death of Sena I after a reign of 20 years. Sena II, nephew of Sena I (son of Kassapa), ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over northern Sri Lanka (Jaffna Peninsula) during the reign of King Sena II.
Lankan expedition sacks Madurai.
Death of Sena II after a reign of 35 years. Udaya I, younger brother of Sena II, ascends the throne.
Death of Udaya I after a reign of 9 years. Kassapa IV, younger brother of Sena II and Udaya I, ascends the throne.
Persian scholar Abu Zayd al-Sirafi compiles accounts of Sri Lanka based on maritime trade networks.
Death of Kassapa IV after a reign of 17 years. Kassapa V, son of Sena II and nephew of Kassapa IV, ascends the throne.
Death of Kassapa V after a reign of 10 years. Dappula IV, son of Kassapa IV, ascends the throne, dies after a reign of 7 months, and Dappula V, younger brother of Dappula IV, ascends the throne.
Death of Dappula V after a reign of 12 years. Udaya II, cousin of Dappula V (son of Udaya I), ascends the throne.
Death of Udaya II after a reign of 3 years. Sena III, brother of Udaya II, ascends the throne.
Death of Sena III after a reign of 3 years. Udaya III, cousin of Sena III (son of Kassapa IV), ascends the throne.
Death of Udaya III after a reign of 3 years. Sena IV, son of Kassapa V, ascends the throne.
Coļas invade Sri Lanka.
Death of Sena IV after a reign of 7 years. Mahinda IV, younger brother of Sena IV, ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over the northern tip of Sri Lanka.
Arab historian and traveler Al-Masudi visits Sri Lanka.
Death of Mahinda IV after a reign of 22 years. Sena V, eldest son of Mahinda IV, ascends the throne.
Total solar eclipse visible over the southern tip of Sri Lanka during the reign of Sena V.
Death of Sena V after a reign of 12 years. Mahinda V, younger brother of Sena V, ascends the throne.
Chola conquest and occupation of Anuradhapura: The Cholas under Rajendra I attack and conquer parts of the Anuradhapura kingdom.

Chola conquest and occupation of Anuradhapura: Death of Mahinda V in captivity in India after 42 nominal years of reign. Kassapa VI (Vikramabahu), son of Mahinda V, leads southern resistance in Ruhuna.
Death of Kassapa VI after a reign of 11 years. Kirti, general under Kassapa VI, reigns in Ruhuna and is slain after 7 days; Mahalana Kitti, noble of Ruhuna, ascends the throne.
Death of Mahalana Kitti after a reign of 3 years; Vikrama Pandya, Pandyan prince living in Ruhuna, reigns.
Death of Vikrama Pandya after a reign of 3 years; Jagathpala, prince of Ayodhya, reigns in Ruhuna.
A Sinhalese chieftain named Lokeshwara, temporarily defeats the Chola forces and establishes a military base in Ruhuna.
The bhikkhu and bhikkhuni monastic communities at Anuradhapura die out following invasions from South India.
Death of Jagathpala after a reign of 6 years; Parakrama Pandya, Pandyan prince, reigns in Ruhuna.
Death of Parakrama Pandya after a reign of 2 years; Loka, prime minister of Ruhuna, reigns.
Keshadhatu Kasyapa, a pretender to the Sinhalese throne, establishes a dominion in Eastern Ruhuna after driving away Chola forces, which would last until 1055.
Death of Loka after a reign of 1 year; Vijayabahu I, royal prince of the Lambakanna lineage, ascends the throne in Ruhuna, expels the Chola Empire, and unifies Sri Lanka at Polonnaruwa.
Prince Kitti, who was given the title Vijayabahu, launches a seventeen-year campaign and successfully drives out the Cholas from Sri Lanka.
Vijayabāhu I expels Colas from the island.
Construction of the stone Buddha sculptures at Gal Vihara following the expulsion of Chola forces from Polonnaruwa.

Velakkara Revolt: Tamil mercenaries named Velakkaras, mutiny against king Vijayabahu as he declared war with the Chola Empire due to arresting a group of Sinhalese ambassadors sent to Western Chalukya.

In Myanmar, during the reign of Kyansittha, completes the building of the Shwezigon Pagoda, a shrine for relics of the Buddha, including a tooth brought from Sri Lanka. Various inscriptions refer to him as an incarnation of Vishnu, a chakravartin, a bodhisattva, and dharmaraja.

Death of Vijayabahu I after a reign of 55 years, and the instalment of Jayabahu I as his successor without passing the throne to Vijayabahu son Vikramabahu I causes a power struggle between the two rulers.
Deposition of Jayabahu I after a reign of 1 year; Vikramabahu I, son of Vijayabahu I, ascends the throne.
Death of Vikramabahu I after a reign of 21 years. Gajabahu II, son of Vikramabahu I, ascends the throne.
A revolt led-by Queen Sugala of Ruhuna against the Parakramabahu I. The rebellion was suppressed by the army and the kingdom of Ruhuna was annexed as a part of Polonnaruwa in 1158.
Ruhuna Rebellion
With the guidance of two forest monks – Ven. Mahākassapa Thera and Ven. Sāriputta Thera, Parakramabahu I reunites all bhikkhus in Sri Lanka into the Mahavihara sect.
Rajarata Rebellion
Anawrahta of Pagan upon request of Vijayabahu I sends monks and scriptures to restart Buddhism in the Sri Lanka.
Death of Parakramabahu I after a reign of 33 years. Vijayabahu II, nephew of Parakramabahu I, ascends the throne.
Vijayabahu II is murdered after a reign of 1 year; Mahinda VI, Kalinga noble, usurps the throne, is slain after 5 days, and Nissanka Malla, prince of Kalinga lineage, ascends the throne.
